newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris says Fla ruling contrary to law.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris says Fla ruling contrary to law.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc said on Monday that a ruling by a Florida judge limiting its ability to use Florida's history of cigarette-making in state prisons in its defense against a lawsuit appears contrary to state and federal law.

In a statement, the tobacco company said it was reviewing the ruling issued Monday by Palm Beach County Circuit Judge Harold Cohen, but at first reading it appeared to be contrary to law and the company was examining avenues of review.

"Of course neither the court nor the Legislature has the authority to strike federally guaranteed defenses such as preemption and we intend to assert those in the case," Philip Morris senor assistant general counsel Gregory Little said.
"In addition, the companies intend to present an aggressive defense relating to the state's conduct and knowledge regarding cigarettes and smoking," he said.

In the ruling, issued in West Palm Beach, Florida, Cohen dismissed a motion brought by Philip Morris Cos and other tobacco groups that they should be allowed to present evidence Florida had made and sold cigarettes in its prisons in a trial scheduled to begin on August 4.
The ruling effectively knocked down "affirmative defenses" -- in which a defendant seeks to avoid liability by showing a plaintiff shares responsibility for harm.
The ruling came on a pre-trial motion in Florida's pioneering lawsuit seeking $1 billion or more in damages for treating state residents with smoking sicknesses.
